domain_label: Micro-Story & Emotion — Expression and Emotion Direction for AI-Generated Performers (FACS vocabulary, the basic-emotions debate, show-not-tell under silent autoplay)
purpose: A method for the expression-and-emotion work an art director reasons about when writing performance direction into image/video prompts for two AI-generated luxury personas: using FACS Action Units as an emotion-agnostic, muscle-level public prompt vocabulary for faces (the Duchenne AU6+AU12 anti-AI-grin lever), carrying the basic-emotions debate honestly so a prompted face is never claimed as a universal signal, directing micro-expression restraint for subtle acting, designing the four emotional beats (aspiration, curiosity gap, tension-release, awe) with their sourced psychology, encoding show-not-tell so the story is legible under muted autoplay, and translating status/ease/confidence body language into per-beat expression choices for a quiet-luxury male and female persona.
assumptions: no observed engagement dataset is supplied; every score is a heuristic prior and every empirical claim is quoted at the honesty tag the grounding research file carries (FACT / FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-craft-doctrine / UNKNOWN), never upgraded

FACS Action Unit labels are quoted as standard textbook FACS (Ekman, Friesen & Hager 2002; ~44 AUs, A-E intensity scale) as the research file cites them; they are used as a description language, not as proof a face signals a universal emotion

the basic-emotions question is treated as genuinely unresolved: Ekman's six/seven, Jack et al. 2014's four, and Barrett's constructed-emotion view are all carried as live positions, and emotion labels are shorthand for a desired reading only

muted-viewing generality rests on the Digiday 2016 '~85% watched without sound' figure, which is publisher-reported and 2016-specific; the load-bearing claim is 'a large majority of first-exposure viewing is muted', not the exact percentage

the personas are fully AI-generated fictional characters; the closed likeness lane stays closed - no direction ever aims to evoke a specific real named person while concealing the face, and celebrity-adjacency legality is out of scope (media-manager/legal file)
exclusions: the model-specific prompt syntax, model ids, parameters, durations and aspect ratios for Higgsfield generators - those come only from the higgsfield_surface file and belong to the prompt-craft specialist, not this expression/emotion layer
camera framing, reveal-shot grammar, stitch transitions and edit rhythm - the camera & editing file's domain, referenced only where a beat needs a reveal
score/voice generation tooling and the soundtrack that carries tension-release audibly - the audio file's domain; voice-delivery direction is included only as the 'phonics' interpretation
posting cadence, algorithm ranking signals, and the attraction/parasocial psychology of the audience - the media-manager file's domain
wardrobe/set construction mechanics and character-consistency (face/identity lock) mechanics - the character/wardrobe file's domain; only the narrative and expression reading of quiet-luxury is here
any guidance for evoking a specific real person while hiding the face, and any deception/lie-detection claim built on micro-expressions

competency_questions.question: Why write facial performance as FACS Action Units instead of emotion labels, and which single AU pairing most improves anti-AI realism?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FACS_AU_VOCABULARY explains AUs as an emotion-agnostic muscle-level language (AU1/2/4/5/6/7/9/12/15/23/26 with the A-E intensity scale) and DUCHENNE_MARKER states the genuine smile is AU6+AU12 while a posed smile is AU12 without AU6, and that prompting eye involvement (AU6) is the highest-leverage fix for the dead-eyed synthetic grin

competency_questions.question: How is the basic-emotions debate carried so a prompted face is never over-claimed as a universal signal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASIC_EMOTIONS_DEBATE names Ekman's six/seven, Jack et al. 2014's four, and Barrett's constructed-emotion view as an unresolved disagreement, and EMOTION_LABEL_AS_SHORTHAND states the working rule: direct AU mechanics and treat any emotion word as shorthand for the desired reading, never as a scientific universality claim

competency_questions.question: How are micro-expressions used as an acting direction given that true 1/25s leakage cannot be reliably shown in a stitched clip?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MICRO_EXPRESSION_RESTRAINT states Ekman & Friesen's 1/25-1/5 second definition, that true micro-expressions are below stitched-clip resolution, that the deception-detection claim is contested and dropped, and that the usable form is prompting restrained 'almost' expressions (a flicker of a smile, a brief eye softening) that read as class for luxury personas

competency_questions.question: Why does awe/high-arousal emotion earn the reveal beat, and what is the sourced basis?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AWE_HIGH_AROUSAL_BEAT cites Berger & Milkman 2012 (JMR) that high-arousal emotions - positive awe, negative anger/anxiety - are more viral while low-arousal sadness is less viral, and applies it to luxury reveal/scale/grandeur as the shareable quadrant

competency_questions.question: How is a curiosity gap opened and closed across a reel, and where is the open loop deliberately left unfilled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CURIOSITY_GAP_BEAT cites Loewenstein 1994 info-gap theory and directs opening on a perceived-fillable gap withholding the fill to the payoff, and OPEN_LOOP_ENDING states the cliffhanger leaves the gap unfilled to drive comments/follows without tipping into never-filled clickbait

competency_questions.question: What is the tension-release engine of held attention and how does a per-beat expression carry it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TENSION_RELEASE_BEAT states that building a small tension (an unfinished motion, an approaching reveal, a rising swell) and releasing it on the payoff is the attention engine, that a reel with none reads as a slideshow, and that expression carries it via a held restrained face resolving into a beat of release

competency_questions.question: What does aspiration mean as a beat and how is a 'this could be you' moment directed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASPIRATION_BEAT states aspiration is desired-self projection (not a basic emotion), directs proximity (first-person 'come with me'), attainability signaling and identity cues, and requires at least one 'this could be you' moment per reel with the expression reading as invitation not gloating

competency_questions.question: Why must the story be fully legible muted, and what does that force on expression and text?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SILENT_AUTOPLAY_LEGIBILITY states first-exposure viewing is mostly muted (Digiday 2016 ~85%, tagged publisher-reported/2016) so meaning must carry visually with captions and a text hook and sound-on payoff as a bonus, and SHOW_NOT_TELL directs replacing stated emotion with depicted AU-level behavior (show the unhurried walk and direct gaze, not the caption 'confident')

competency_questions.question: How is status read as quiet vs loud, and which register do the classic-luxury personas occupy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STATUS_QUIET_VS_LOUD cites Han, Nunes & Dreze 2010 brand-prominence taxonomy (Patrician/Parvenu/Proletarian/Poseur) placing classic-luxury in the Patrician quiet-signal register, and BODY_LANGUAGE_VOCABULARY gives the ease/confidence body cues (unhurried movement, open posture, reduced blink, stillness) that encode status without loud signals

competency_questions.question: How do aloofness and controlled non-revelation function as luxury devices without crossing into evoking a specific real person?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ALOOFNESS_NON_REVELATION states scarcity of self-disclosure (restrained expression, gaze control, partial obscuring, back-to-camera) reads as exclusivity and serves the face-not-revealed idea, and LIKENESS_CLOSED_LANE holds that non-revelation must never be used to evoke a specific named real person while hiding the face - that lane stays closed

competency_questions.question: How is voice delivery ('phonics') directed for a voiceover luxury persona?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VOICE_DELIVERY_PHONICS interprets the owner's 'phonics' as voice-delivery (flagged as interpretation not certainty), gives the ~140-160 wpm target (NCVS ~150 wpm conversational anchor), downward-resolving pitch for authority, and strategic pauses aligned to cut points, as an enhancement for the minority who unmute

competency_questions.question: How are the two personas differentiated by per-beat expression choice while both staying quiet-luxury?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERSONA_EXPRESSION_MAP assigns each persona a distinct but quiet-register expression signature (e.g. the male grounded low-register stillness, the female composed warmth with restrained AU6) mapped to hook/escalation/payoff beats, and DUAL_PERSONA_INTERPLAY designs the complementary paired-format relational thread without breaking either signature

competency_questions.question: How is the whole expression/emotion direction composed into a per-beat performance brief that stays honest and muted-legible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERFORMANCE_BRIEF_COMPOSITION composes AU-level direction, the honest emotion-label rule, the four beats, show-not-tell, body language and per-persona signatures into one per-beat brief and conditions any brief on muted-legibility and the no-real-person-evocation rule

competency_questions.question: Which emotional register does story design optimize for given the shares/sends reach driver?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states that because shareable reach favors high-arousal awe (Berger & Milkman), the performance brief biases toward awe-and-aspiration reveals over low-arousal registers, while keeping the honesty and muted-legibility constraints

glossary.definition: A unit of the Facial Action Coding System that names a facial movement by its underlying muscle action rather than by an emotion; ~44 AUs with a 5-point A-E intensity scale, e.g. AU6 cheek raiser (orbicularis oculi), AU12 lip corner puller (zygomaticus major), AU4 brow lowerer [FACT - standard FACS, Ekman/Friesen/Hager 2002 as the research file cites]. Used here as an emotion-agnostic prompt vocabulary.

The smile that combines AU6 (cheek raiser, eye crinkle) with AU12 (lip corner puller); a posed/social smile is AU12 without AU6. Prompting for the eye involvement of AU6 is the single highest-leverage direction against the dead-eyed synthetic AI grin [FACT - textbook FACS/Duchenne distinction].

The unresolved scientific disagreement over whether emotions are innate universal kinds: Ekman's six (happiness, sadness, fear, anger, surprise, disgust) or seven (+contempt); Jack, Garrod & Schyns 2014 arguing four at the biologically-rooted level; Barrett's Theory of Constructed Emotion holding that only affect (valence x arousal) is innate and specific emotions are constructed [FACT - all three positions carried as live].

A very fast involuntary facial movement lasting 1/25 to 1/5 of a second, termed by Ekman & Friesen as leakage of concealed emotion [FACT - Paul Ekman Group]. The deception-detection use is contested and is not adopted; the usable form for prompting is directed restraint - a flicker of an 'almost' expression.

Emotions high on the activation axis; Berger & Milkman 2012 (Journal of Marketing Research, all NYT articles over ~3 months) found high-arousal content - positive awe, negative anger/anxiety - more viral, while low-arousal deactivating emotion (sadness) is less viral [FACT]. Awe is the aspirational high-arousal quadrant luxury reveals live in.

Loewenstein 1994 (Psychological Bulletin 116(1):75-98): curiosity is a cognitively induced deprivation from a perceived gap between what one knows and wants to know, intensifying with how fillable the gap feels [FACT]. Opened at the hook and closed at the payoff, or left unfilled as an open loop.

Reels autoplay muted by default; the '~85% of Facebook video watched without sound' figure is Digiday 2016 (Sahil Patel), publisher-reported and 2016-specific [FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-generality]. The load-bearing claim is that a large majority of first-exposure viewing is muted, forcing full visual legibility.

Han, Nunes & Dreze 2010 (Journal of Marketing 74:15-30): a taxonomy of Patricians (quiet signals for insiders), Parvenus (loud conspicuous signals), Proletarians (don't signal), Poseurs (counterfeit) [FACT]; loud goods averaged cheaper. Classic-luxury sits in the Patrician quiet register - understated cut, no loud logos, if-you-know-you-know.

Replacing stated emotion with depicted AU-level behavior and body language so a muted viewer reads the story from the image alone - show the unhurried walk, direct gaze and relaxed shoulders instead of captioning 'confident' [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine], dovetailing with FACS mechanical direction.

The owner's speech-to-text word 'phonics' read here as voice-delivery direction (interpretation, not certainty): pace ~140-160 wpm against the NCVS ~150 wpm conversational anchor [FACT for the wpm], downward-resolving pitch for authority and strategic pauses at cut points [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine] - an enhancement for the minority who unmute.

nodes.definition: Adopt the Facial Action Coding System's Action Units as the public, emotion-agnostic vocabulary for writing facial performance into prompts. FACS categorizes facial movement by the underlying muscle action; it defines on the order of ~44 AUs each on a 5-point A-E intensity scale, rooted in Hjortsjo's anatomy and adapted by Ekman, Friesen & Hager (1978; 2002 update) [FACT - standard FACS as the research file cites, sources 3/3a/3b]. The load-bearing illustrative AUs for direction are AU1 inner brow raiser, AU2 outer brow raiser, AU4 brow lowerer (concentration/frown), AU5 upper lid raiser, AU6 cheek raiser (the eye part of a genuine smile), AU7 lid tightener, AU9 nose wrinkler, AU12 lip corner puller (the smile muscle), AU15 lip corner depressor, AU23 lip tightener, AU26 jaw drop. Directing the mechanics ('AU6 cheeks lifting, eyes crinkling') instead of the label ('happy') reads more photoreal and is what the rest of this KB's expression work builds on.

included: AUs as an emotion-agnostic muscle-level description language
the illustrative AU1..AU26 vocabulary and the A-E intensity scale
why mechanical direction beats label direction for realism
excluded: the Duchenne AU6+AU12 anti-grin lever specifically (its own node)
the model-specific syntax that renders an AU direction (prompt-craft specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a model's AU fidelity or a FACS revision changes the vocabulary

pros.claim: An emotion-agnostic muscle-level vocabulary lets a specialist direct anatomy rather than invoke a stereotype, which reads more photoreal
pros.example: prompting 'AU4 slight brow lower, AU7 lid tighten, neutral mouth' for cool focus instead of the plastic label 'serious'

cons.claim: FACS is a description system for observed movement, not a rendering guarantee - a generator may not honor a named AU faithfully
cons.example: prompting AU6 cheek raise and still getting a lip-only grin because the model ignores the eye direction

failure_modes: prompting emotion labels ('happy', 'sad') and inheriting the plastic AI-stereotype face

nodes.definition: Carry the basic-emotions controversy honestly, because it governs how far an expression direction may claim. Three live positions: the classical Ekman view of biologically hardwired basic emotions, commonly six (happiness, sadness, fear, anger, surprise, disgust) sometimes seven (+contempt), with cross-culturally recognizable faces [FACT - sources 4/3b]; Jack, Garrod & Schyns 2014 (Current Biology) arguing expressions are segmented over time and support four basic categories at the biologically-rooted level (fear/surprise and anger/disgust initially share signals) [FACT - sources 4a/4b/4c]; and Barrett's Theory of Constructed Emotion, which holds only affect (valence x arousal) is innate and specific emotions are constructed from prediction, interoception and learned concepts, citing the lack of consistent facial/neural/physiological signatures [FACT - source 4d, Barrett 2017/2025]. The disagreement is genuine and unresolved. An expert therefore never asserts a prompted face is a universal emotional signal.

included: Ekman six/seven, Jack et al. four, and Barrett constructed-emotion as three live positions
that the disagreement is unresolved
that faces cannot be claimed as universal signals
excluded: the working prompt rule that follows from it (its own node)
the FACS AU mechanics themselves (its own node)

pros.claim: Holding the debate open keeps expression direction defensible and prevents over-claiming a rendered face as a universal signal
pros.example: describing 'the reading is meant to land as calm confidence' rather than asserting the face universally signals happiness

cons.claim: The unresolved science gives no single authoritative emotion-to-face mapping to lean on, so direction must stay at the mechanical/affect level
cons.example: being unable to guarantee a cross-cultural 'this is fear' face and having to specify AUs and context instead

nodes.definition: Fix the working rule that resolves the debate for practice: direct the AU mechanics and treat any emotion word only as shorthand for the desired reading, never as a scientific claim that the face is a universal signal. Concretely, a brief writes 'AU6+AU12 low intensity, gaze soft - reads as warm ease' rather than 'happy'; the label rides along as a human-readable target while the anatomy does the work. This is the honest synthesis the research file lands on, and it conveniently also produces more photoreal output because it specifies muscles not stereotypes [FACT-derived synthesis of sources 3/4]. The rule binds every downstream beat and persona node: emotion vocabulary is allowed as communication shorthand, but the prompt content is AU-level and affect-level.

nodes.definition: Apply the single highest-leverage expression direction for anti-AI realism: the Duchenne (genuine) smile is AU6 (cheek raiser, eyes crinkling) plus AU12 (lip corner puller), whereas a social/posed smile is AU12 without AU6 [FACT - textbook FACS/Duchenne distinction]. Generators left to default produce the dead-eyed synthetic grin because they render the mouth (AU12) and neglect the eye involvement (AU6). Explicitly prompting the AU6 component - 'eyes crinkling, cheeks lifting, warmth reaching the eyes' - is the concrete fix. For the luxury register this is used at low intensity: a restrained genuine warmth, not a broad grin. This node operationalizes DUCHENNE for every warm beat and both personas.

nodes.definition: Convert the micro-expression concept into a usable restraint direction. Ekman & Friesen termed involuntary facial movements lasting 1/25 to 1/5 of a second micro-expressions - brief leakage of concealed emotion [FACT - Paul Ekman Group, source 12]. Two honesty caveats: the deception/lie-detection claims attached to micro-expressions are contested and are NOT adopted here; and a true 1/25s movement is below what a 3-6s stitched clip reliably resolves. What survives as craft is the concept of restraint: prompt for subtle 'almost' expressions - 'the faintest smile beginning at the lip corners', 'a brief softening of the eyes', 'a near-imperceptible chin lift'. For luxury personas restraint reads as class while broad expression reads as trying-too-hard, so micro-direction is the default register, not the exception.

nodes.definition: Anchor the constraint that governs all expression work: reels autoplay muted and a large majority of first-exposure viewing is watched without sound. The most-cited figure - '~85% of Facebook video watched without sound' - is Digiday 2016 (Sahil Patel), a publisher-reported range (LittleThings/Mic/MEC ~85-90%), corroborated by Nieman Lab and Marketing Dive [FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-generality: publishers said ~85%, it is a 2016 figure, not a current universal platform metric]. The load-bearing claim - independent of the exact percentage - is that first exposure is mostly muted, so the story must be fully legible with sound off. That forces meaning onto expression, body language, action, environment and on-screen text; any spoken content must be captioned; a bold text hook covers seconds 0-2; and a sound-on payoff (a score drop, a whispered line) is a bonus for the minority who unmute, never a dependency.

nodes.definition: Design the awe beat as the shareable high-arousal register. Berger & Milkman (2012), Journal of Marketing Research, analyzing all New York Times articles over ~3 months, found content evoking high-arousal emotions - positive awe, negative anger and anxiety - is more viral, while low-arousal deactivating emotion such as sadness is less viral; positive beats negative on average but arousal is the mechanism, holding controlling for surprise, interest, usefulness and placement [FACT - source 6]. For the luxury operation this makes sweeping reveals, scale and grandeur - the car door opening, the penthouse reveal, the summit vista - awe machines that sit in exactly the aspirational high-arousal quadrant. The expression that carries awe is AU1+AU2 (brow raise), slight AU5 (upper lid raise), a low AU26 (lips parting) at restrained intensity - quiet awe, not a gasp. This beat is the reach engine the whole brief biases toward.

nodes.definition: Design the curiosity-gap beat that wins the hook. Loewenstein (1994), 'The Psychology of Curiosity', Psychological Bulletin 116(1):75-98, gives information-gap theory: curiosity is a cognitively induced deprivation arising from a perceived gap between what one knows and wants to know, and its intensity rises with how fillable the gap feels [FACT - source 5]. In practice the reel opens on a gap - what is behind this door, where does this road go, what happens at the end - and withholds the fill until the payoff. The expression carries the gap by directing the persona's gaze off-frame or toward the unrevealed thing (an off-screen look, a hand on an unopened door) so the viewer inherits the question. The discipline: the gap must feel fillable and must actually be filled at the payoff - over-teasing a gap that never fills is clickbait that breeds distrust.

nodes.definition: Design the tension-release beat, the universal engine of held attention. Build a small tension - an unfinished motion, an approaching reveal, a rising musical swell - and release it on the payoff; a reel with no tension-release reads as a slideshow [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine, source in research file]. In a stitched reel the edit rhythm and score carry most of the tension, but the performance carries its share: a held, restrained face (AU7 lid tighten, AU23 lip tighten, stillness) during the build that resolves into a beat of release (a breath out, shoulders dropping, the restrained genuine AU6+AU12) at the payoff. The tension expression and the release expression are a matched pair authored together, and the release is aligned to the payoff cut so the visual, the score and the face resolve on the same frame.

nodes.definition: Design the aspiration beat as desired-self projection. Aspiration is not one of the classic basic emotions; it works by letting the viewer imagine themselves in the persona's position [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine, source 14 area]. The levers are proximity (first-person 'come with me' POV, the viewer's-eye arrival), attainability signaling (make the lifestyle feel reachable, not merely observed), and identity cues that match the target audience's ideal self. Every reel should contain at least one 'this could be you' moment. The expression that carries aspiration reads as invitation, not gloating: an open, direct-but-soft gaze to camera (a restrained AU6 warmth, relaxed brow) that includes the viewer rather than performing superiority over them. This beat pairs with awe (the reveal is the aspiration) and is the emotional bridge between the persona and the audience's self-image.

included: aspiration as desired-self projection (not a basic emotion)
proximity/attainability/identity levers and the 'this could be you' moment
the invitation-not-gloating expression reading
excluded: the deeper attraction/parasocial psychology (media-manager file)
the awe reveal itself (its own node)

nodes.definition: Encode the show-not-tell craft that muted autoplay demands: replace stated emotion with depicted behavior so a muted viewer reads the story from the image alone [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. Do not caption 'she is confident' - show the unhurried walk, the direct gaze with reduced blink, the relaxed shoulders. Do not caption 'he is at ease' - show the slow exhale, the loose hands, the stillness. This dovetails with the FACS layer: express through AU-level mechanics and body language, not labels, which is the same discipline as EMOTION_LABEL_AS_SHORTHAND applied to the whole frame. Where spoken content is essential it becomes on-screen text (which also serves accessibility); where a text hook is needed it carries the first 1-2 seconds. Show-not-tell is what makes the four beats legible without sound.

AU-level and body-language expression as the delivery
on-screen text/caption only where speech is essential
excluded: the specific body-language status cues (its own node)
the muted-viewing evidence itself (its own node)

pros.example: showing an unhurried walk and steady gaze to convey confidence instead of the caption 'confident'

cons.example: a restrained ease read as boredom by a viewer with no captioned or contextual anchor

nodes.definition: Provide the body-language vocabulary for status, ease and confidence that carries the read below the face. The load-bearing cues [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]: unhurried movement and deliberate pace (rushing reads as low status), open and settled posture (uncrossed, shoulders down and back), reduced blink and steady gaze (confidence), stillness and economy of motion (ease - the calm body does not fidget), and controlled gesture (few, deliberate hand movements rather than many). These pair with the facial AUs: a calm confident face over a fidgeting body is incoherent. For the quiet-luxury register the body language is the primary status signal - because loud logos are excluded (STATUS_QUIET_VS_LOUD), the posture, pace and stillness do the status work. This vocabulary feeds show-not-tell and the per-persona signatures.

included: unhurried pace, open posture, reduced blink, stillness, controlled gesture as status/ease/confidence cues
coherence between body and facial AUs
body language as the primary quiet-luxury status signal
excluded: the quiet-vs-loud brand-prominence theory (its own node)
the per-persona assignment of these cues (persona node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a body/face incoherence or a register change updates the vocabulary

pros.claim: A concrete body-cue vocabulary lets status and ease be directed below the face where the quiet-luxury signal actually lives
pros.example: directing an unhurried gait, settled shoulders and reduced blink to read high-status without any logo

cons.claim: Body cues can contradict the face if authored separately, producing an incoherent read
cons.example: a calm confident face over fidgeting hands and a rushed walk that reads as anxious, not at ease

failure_modes: authoring the face and body separately so they contradict
reading rushed or fidgeting movement as high status
revisit_triggers: a body/face incoherence surfaces in output review

nodes.definition: Fix the status register the personas occupy. Han, Nunes & Dreze (2010), 'Signaling Status with Luxury Goods: The Role of Brand Prominence', Journal of Marketing 74:15-30, introduces brand prominence (how conspicuous the mark is) and a four-group taxonomy: Patricians (wealthy, low need for status - quiet signals only insiders recognize), Parvenus (wealthy, high need - loud conspicuous signals to distance from have-nots), Proletarians (do not signal), Poseurs (aspirational, counterfeit to mimic parvenus); empirically loud prominently-branded goods averaged cheaper than quiet ones across 465 handbags [FACT - source 15]. The owner's classic-luxurious aesthetic is the Patrician / quiet-luxury register: understated tailoring, no loud logos, materials-and-craft over branding, if-you-know-you-know. Quiet signals read as higher status to in-group audiences; the Parvenu/Poseur loud-logo register is avoided as reading lower and new-money. This governs how expression and body language are calibrated - restraint over display.

included: Han/Nunes/Dreze brand-prominence taxonomy and the quiet<loud status finding
classic-luxury as the Patrician quiet register
restraint-over-display as the calibration rule
excluded: the wardrobe/set mechanics that render quiet luxury (character/wardrobe file)
the aloofness non-revelation devices (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a register drift or a positioning revision updates the status calibration

pros.claim: Grounding the register in a real study gives a defensible reason to choose restraint over loud display
pros.example: directing understated cut and no visible logo because quiet signals read as higher status to the in-group

cons.claim: The quiet register is easy to misread as plain or low-effort if the craft cues (materials, cut, restraint) are not legible
cons.example: an understated look with no visible craft reading as merely cheap rather than quietly expensive

failure_modes: drifting into the Parvenu loud-logo register that reads as new-money
rendering quiet luxury as plain so it reads as low-effort rather than high-status
revisit_triggers: a persona drifts toward loud-logo display
the quiet register reads as plain rather than premium
the brand-prominence positioning is revised

nodes.definition: Direct aloofness and controlled non-revelation as luxury devices. Scarcity of self-disclosure is a status signal - the persona that reveals less reads as more exclusive [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. Devices: restrained expression (micro not macro - MICRO_EXPRESSION_RESTRAINT), gaze control (looking away, or a cool direct gaze rather than an eager one), not-explaining (letting the image stand), and controlled reveal (the face partially obscured, the back-to-camera contemplative shot). For the cool aloof face specifically: reduced AU12, a slight AU4, neutral-to-lowered lids, minimal expressiveness - the 'quiet face'. This grammar also serves the owner's face-not-revealed idea and is the same visual language as quiet luxury: aloofness and non-revelation are one register. It is directed with restraint so it reads as exclusive composure, not coldness or absence.

included: scarcity of self-disclosure as a status signal
restrained expression, gaze control, not-explaining, controlled/partial reveal
the reduced-AU12 slight-AU4 cool 'quiet face'
excluded: the closed-lane rule against evoking a real person (its own node)
the legal celebrity-adjacency boundary (legal file)

pros.claim: Non-revelation devices double as exclusivity signals and as the face-not-revealed grammar the owner asked for
pros.example: a back-to-camera contemplative reveal that reads as exclusive and keeps the face out of frame at once

cons.claim: Aloofness overshot reads as cold or absent and can break the aspiration invitation
cons.example: so much non-revelation and cool distance that the persona feels unreachable and the 'this could be you' bond never forms

failure_modes: aloofness overshooting into coldness that kills the aspiration bond

revisit_triggers: aloofness reads as cold and breaks the aspiration bond in review

nodes.definition: Hold the closed likeness lane closed. The personas are fully AI-generated fictional characters; non-revelation and face-obscuring devices (ALOOFNESS_NON_REVELATION) must NEVER be used to evoke a specific named real person while hiding the face. There is no direction anywhere in this KB - not in aloofness, not in persona design, not in the 'famous-people' framing - that aims to make a persona read as a particular real individual under cover of concealment. The face-not-revealed idea is served only by original, non-identifying composition. Celebrity-adjacency legality itself is out of scope here (media-manager/legal file); this node is the expression-side guardrail that keeps every performance direction on original fictional characters. Any brief that starts to steer toward a recognizable real person is stopped at this node.

the rule that non-revelation must not evoke a specific real person
stopping any brief that steers toward a recognizable individual
excluded: the legal analysis of celebrity-adjacency (legal file)

pros.example: rejecting a brief that uses a back-to-camera shot plus signature styling to imply a specific celebrity

cons.claim: The guardrail requires judgment about what counts as 'evoking a specific person', which can be a gray line for archetypes
cons.example: distinguishing a generic 'old-money' archetype from a concealed evocation of one identifiable individual

nodes.definition: Direct voice delivery as the working interpretation of the owner's 'phonics'. The word 'phonics' is a speech-to-text artifact in a story-levels list; read here as voice-delivery for voiceover reels, flagged as an interpretation not a certainty [UNKNOWN-artifact resolved to a working reading]. Pace: average conversational English is ~150 wpm (National Center for Voice and Speech, via source 16), audiobook/podcast narration ~150-160 wpm; a reel voiceover aims for ~140-160 wpm - crisp but natural, with slower than ~130 reading ponderous and faster than ~170 rushed [FACT for the wpm anchors, ESTIMATE for the reel band]. Pitch: vary to avoid monotone, favor a grounded lower register with downward-resolving phrase ends that read as authoritative for a luxury-authority persona [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. Pause: strategic silence before a key word or the payoff creates emphasis and, aligned to cut points, lets a just-unmuted viewer catch up. Because most first exposure is muted, voice is an enhancement for the minority who unmute, never the load-bearer.

included: the 'phonics'->voice-delivery interpretation flagged as such
the ~140-160 wpm band on the ~150 wpm anchor, downward-resolving pitch, strategic pauses at cuts
voice as enhancement not load-bearer under muted autoplay
excluded: the voice-generation tooling (audio file)
the score/music that also carries tension (audio file)

pros.example: specifying ~150 wpm, lower register, downward phrase-ends and a pause before the payoff word

cons.claim: 'Phonics' is an interpretation, so building heavy delivery doctrine on it risks answering a question the owner did not ask
cons.example: over-investing in voiceover direction when the owner meant something else by 'phonics'

failure_modes: treating the 'phonics' interpretation as certain rather than a flagged reading
making the voiceover load-bearing when most first exposure is muted
revisit_triggers: the owner clarifies what 'phonics' meant

nodes.definition: Assign each of the two personas a distinct but quiet-register expression signature mapped to the hook/escalation/payoff beats, so the male and female read as different characters without either leaving the Patrician register. Illustrative signatures [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine on the quiet-luxury base]: the male persona - grounded low-register stillness, a cool direct gaze (slight AU4, reduced AU12, reduced blink), warmth rationed to a restrained AU6 flicker at the payoff; the female persona - composed warmth, a softer AU6-led restraint (eyes leading the smile) with the same unhurried body language and controlled gesture. Per beat: at the hook each opens on their signature stillness/gaze that carries the curiosity gap; through escalation the restraint holds; at the payoff each releases their rationed warmth (the male a smaller move, the female an eye-led one). Both stay muted-legible via show-not-tell and both obey the no-real-person rule. The signatures are consistent across posts so the personas read as continuous characters.

the hook/escalation/payoff mapping of each signature
consistency of signatures across posts
excluded: the paired dual-persona relational thread (its own node)
the face/identity-lock consistency mechanics (character/wardrobe file)

nodes.definition: Synthesize the four emotional beats and the show-not-tell/body-language craft into the raw material each persona signature draws on, before the signatures are assigned. This node collects: the awe expression (AU1/2/5/26 restrained), the curiosity-gap gaze direction, the tension-release matched pair, the aspiration invitation gaze, the show-not-tell behavioral delivery and the body-language status cues - and states that a persona signature is a consistent selection across these that fits the quiet register. It is the bridge between the beat/craft layer and the per-persona assignment: without a single collected palette, two signatures would be authored ad hoc and risk incoherence with the beats. The synthesis keeps each persona's hook/escalation/payoff choices drawn from the same sourced beat vocabulary rather than invented per reel.

nodes.definition: Design the dual-persona interplay: the male and female personas appear in complementary or paired formats as a recurring relational thread the audience follows, without either breaking their individual signature (PERSONA_EXPRESSION_MAP). The interplay is expressive, not narrative-heavy - a paired arrival, a complementary two-shot, an answered-look across a cut - and reads through expression and body language under muted autoplay (show-not-tell). Each persona keeps their quiet-register signature; the relationship is carried by matched pacing, reciprocal gaze, and complementary composition rather than dialogue a muted viewer cannot hear. The thread gives the account a relational spine across posts and both personas still obey the no-real-person rule and the quiet-luxury register. It is the highest-composition expression unit because it must keep two signatures coherent at once.

nodes.definition: Design the open-loop ending as a deliberately unfilled curiosity gap (CURIOSITY_GAP_BEAT) that drives comments and follows rather than a rewatch. Where a hard loop closes the story by matching the last frame to the first for invisible replay, the open loop ends on an unresolved beat - a 'part 2', a numbered series ('Location 3 of 7'), a withheld reveal - that converts single-view curiosity into subscription. The expression that carries an open loop is a held, unresolved face (the restrained anticipation of MICRO_EXPRESSION_RESTRAINT, gaze toward the still-unrevealed thing) rather than a released payoff. The discipline from the curiosity-gap node still binds: the gap must feel fillable and the series must eventually pay it off across posts - a promised part 2 that never arrives is the clickbait failure that erodes trust. Choose open loop vs hard loop per format.

nodes.definition: Compose the whole expression/emotion layer into a single per-beat performance brief and gate it on honesty and muted legibility. The brief, for each beat of a reel, specifies: the AU-level facial direction (FACS_AU_VOCABULARY, DUCHENNE_MARKER at low intensity), the emotion label only as reading shorthand (EMOTION_LABEL_AS_SHORTHAND), the intended beat emotion (awe, curiosity gap, tension-release, aspiration), the show-not-tell behavioral delivery and body-language status cues, the per-persona signature (PERSONA_EXPRESSION_MAP) and any dual-persona interplay, plus the ending mode (open loop or hard loop). Two hard gates bind every brief: it must be fully legible muted (SILENT_AUTOPLAY_LEGIBILITY / SHOW_NOT_TELL), and it must never evoke a specific real person (LIKENESS_CLOSED_LANE). Because shareable reach favors high-arousal awe (AWE_HIGH_AROUSAL_BEAT), the composed brief biases toward awe-and-aspiration reveals while keeping restraint, honesty and muted-legibility. This is the deliverable the prompt-craft specialist consumes.

conflict_axes.name: au_mechanics_vs_emotion_label
conflict_axes.description: Writing performance as AU-level muscle mechanics reads more photoreal and stays honest, while reaching for an emotion label is easier but inherits the plastic stereotype and over-claims universality.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always write AU mechanics as the prompt content and keep the emotion word only as a reading target

conflict_axes.name: high_arousal_awe_vs_quiet_restraint
conflict_axes.description: The awe beat wants a high-arousal expressive reveal for shareability while the quiet-luxury register wants restraint; expression intensity is pulled two ways.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: render awe at restrained intensity so the reveal reads inside the Patrician register

conflict_axes.name: aloof_distance_vs_aspirational_invitation
conflict_axes.description: Aloof non-revelation signals exclusivity by distancing while aspiration must invite the viewer to self-insert; distance and inclusion conflict.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep composed aloofness but guarantee one inviting 'this could be you' moment per reel

conflict_axes.name: genuine_warmth_vs_cool_face
conflict_axes.description: The Duchenne genuine-warmth lever and the reduced-AU12 aloof cool face are opposite expression choices that cannot coexist in one frame.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: select per beat and per persona - warmth on payoff/aspiration, cool face on hook/aloof - never both at once

conflict_axes.name: muted_visual_vs_audio_carried
conflict_axes.description: Muted-default first exposure demands fully visual meaning while voice delivery tempts audio-carried meaning the majority never hears.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep all load-bearing meaning visual and captioned; voice is a sound-on bonus only

conflict_axes.name: unfilled_open_loop_vs_filled_gap
conflict_axes.description: The open loop leaves the curiosity gap unfilled to drive follows while the curiosity-gap discipline demands the gap be filled or it becomes clickbait.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow an open loop only if the series pays it off across posts; never leave a gap unfilled everywhere

conflict_axes.name: restraint_subtlety_vs_render_reliability
conflict_axes.description: Directing restrained micro-expression reads as class but is fragile - a generator may under-render it to a flat blank face, losing the beat.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: direct restraint but specify a floor of visible movement (e.g. a low-but-present AU6) so the beat still reads

conflict_axes.name: two_distinct_signatures_vs_one_register
conflict_axes.description: Two personas must read as clearly different people yet both sit inside one narrow quiet-luxury register, risking either blur or a register break.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: differentiate on rationed-warmth size and gaze while holding both in the quiet register

conflict_axes.name: original_character_vs_real_person_evocation
conflict_axes.description: Face-concealing devices serve exclusivity and the face-not-revealed idea but could be misused to evoke a specific real person under cover of concealment.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the closed lane closed - concealment serves only original characters and any real-person evocation is stopped

edge_cases.description: A smile is prompted with only the lip movement so the generator returns the dead-eyed synthetic grin
edge_cases.trigger: AU12 is directed without the AU6 eye-involvement component
edge_cases.mitigation: always name the AU6 cheek-raise/eye-crinkle component on any warm smile and set a low-to-moderate intensity for the luxury register

edge_cases.description: An emotion label is stated in a caption or metadata as if the prompted face were a universal cross-cultural signal
edge_cases.trigger: the reading-shorthand label is treated as a scientific universality claim
edge_cases.mitigation: keep emotion words as internal reading targets only, direct AU mechanics as the content, and never publish the label as a universality claim

edge_cases.description: A reel's core meaning is carried by a voiceover line a muted first-exposure viewer never hears
edge_cases.trigger: audio is made load-bearing under muted-default autoplay
edge_cases.mitigation: carry all load-bearing meaning visually and in captions; keep the voiceover a sound-on enhancement only

edge_cases.description: The 2016 publisher-reported ~85% muted figure is quoted as a current universal platform statistic
edge_cases.trigger: the tagged FACT-of-attribution figure is upgraded to a present-day platform metric
edge_cases.mitigation: quote the figure as Digiday 2016, publisher-reported and 2016-specific, and lean on the general muted-majority claim instead

edge_cases.description: A restrained micro-expression is under-rendered by the generator into a flat, emotionless face and the beat is lost
edge_cases.trigger: the direction specifies subtlety with no floor of visible movement
edge_cases.mitigation: specify a floor of visible movement (a low-but-present AU) so the restrained beat still reads on screen

edge_cases.description: A face-concealing back-to-camera shot plus signature styling is used to imply a specific recognizable celebrity
edge_cases.trigger: concealment devices are steered toward evoking a specific named real person
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the closed lane closed - use concealment only for original fictional characters and stop any brief steering toward a recognizable individual

edge_cases.description: The two personas both drift into the same cool aloof character and read as indistinct
edge_cases.trigger: the per-persona differentiators are too subtle inside the narrow quiet register
edge_cases.mitigation: differentiate on rationed-warmth size, gaze and pacing while keeping both in the quiet register, and check distinctness at hook/escalation/payoff

edge_cases.description: An open-loop 'part 2' is teased and the promised continuation never ships across the series
edge_cases.trigger: an open loop is left unfilled everywhere, not just within one reel
edge_cases.mitigation: only open a loop the series will pay off; track promised continuations and ship them, treating a never-filled gap as disallowed clickbait

edge_cases.description: The awe reveal is rendered as a broad open-mouthed gasp that breaks the quiet-luxury restraint
edge_cases.trigger: the high-arousal awe beat is directed at full intensity
edge_cases.mitigation: render awe at restrained intensity (slight AU1/2/5, low AU26) so the reveal reads as quiet awe inside the Patrician register

edge_cases.description: A calm confident face is authored over a fidgeting, rushed body so the read is incoherent
edge_cases.trigger: facial AUs and body language are authored separately
edge_cases.mitigation: author face and body together so the AUs and the pace/posture/blink cues agree on one read

edge_cases.description: The 'phonics' voice-delivery interpretation is treated as certain and heavy voiceover doctrine is built on a possibly-wrong reading
edge_cases.trigger: the flagged interpretation is taken as the owner's confirmed intent
edge_cases.mitigation: carry 'phonics'->voice-delivery as an explicit interpretation, keep the voiceover investment light, and confirm intent with the owner before scaling it

edge_cases.description: A quiet-luxury look is rendered so plainly it reads as cheap rather than quietly expensive
edge_cases.trigger: restraint is applied without legible craft cues (materials, cut, composure)
edge_cases.mitigation: pair restraint with legible craft and composed body language so the quiet register reads as high-status, not low-effort

workflow.action: Adopt FACS Action Units and the honest emotion-label rule as the expression vocabulary
workflow.description: State AUs as an emotion-agnostic muscle-level language, carry the basic-emotions debate, and fix the direct-AU-mechanics-with-label-as-shorthand rule
workflow.gate: the illustrative AU set, the A-E scale, the three-position debate and the label-as-shorthand rule are stated

workflow.action: Fix the Duchenne anti-grin lever and the micro-expression restraint register
workflow.description: State genuine smile = AU6+AU12 vs posed AU12-only, the AU6 anti-dead-eye fix, and restrained 'almost' expression as the luxury default
workflow.gate: the AU6+AU12 distinction, the eye-involvement fix and the restrained micro register are stated

workflow.action: Anchor muted-autoplay legibility and the show-not-tell craft
workflow.description: State that first exposure is mostly muted (Digiday 2016 ~85%, tagged), that meaning must carry visually with captions and a text hook, and that behavior is depicted not labeled
workflow.gate: the tagged muted figure, the visual-carry rule and the depict-not-label craft are stated

workflow.action: Design the awe/high-arousal beat as the shareable reveal
workflow.description: Cite Berger & Milkman high-arousal virality, place luxury reveals in the aspirational quadrant, and give the restrained awe AUs
workflow.gate: the high-arousal-is-more-viral finding with scope and the restrained awe expression are stated

workflow.action: Design the curiosity-gap and tension-release beats
workflow.description: Cite Loewenstein info-gap theory, direct opening on a fillable gap withheld to the payoff, and author the held-then-released tension pair
workflow.gate: the info-gap basis, the gap-opened-and-filled discipline and the tension-release matched pair are stated

workflow.action: Design the aspiration beat as desired-self invitation
workflow.description: State aspiration as desired-self projection, the proximity/attainability/identity levers, the 'this could be you' moment and the invitation-not-gloating expression
workflow.gate: the desired-self framing, the levers and the invitation expression are stated

workflow.action: Give the body-language vocabulary and the quiet-luxury status register
workflow.description: State the status/ease/confidence body cues, cite Han/Nunes/Dreze brand prominence, and place the personas in the Patrician quiet register
workflow.gate: the body cues, the brand-prominence taxonomy and the quiet-luxury placement are stated

workflow.action: Direct aloofness/non-revelation and hold the closed likeness lane
workflow.description: State the non-revelation devices and the cool face, and the guardrail that concealment never evokes a specific real person
workflow.gate: the non-revelation devices and the no-real-person guardrail are stated

workflow.action: Interpret 'phonics' as voice delivery for the unmute minority
workflow.description: State the flagged interpretation, the ~140-160 wpm band, downward-resolving pitch and strategic pauses, as a sound-on enhancement
workflow.gate: the flagged interpretation, the wpm band and the enhancement-not-load-bearer rule are stated

workflow.action: Assign per-persona signatures and design the dual-persona interplay
workflow.description: Synthesize the beats into a palette, assign each persona a distinct quiet-register signature across hook/escalation/payoff, and design the paired relational thread
workflow.gate: two distinct quiet-register signatures mapped to the beats and a coherent paired interplay are stated

workflow.action: Compose the per-beat performance brief and gate it
workflow.description: Compose AU direction, honest labels, the four beats, show-not-tell, body language, per-persona signatures and the ending mode into one brief, gated muted-legible and no-real-person
workflow.gate: the brief states each beat's AU/reading/persona/ending and passes the muted-legibility and no-real-person gates before handoff

priority_rationale: The foundation nodes come first because every beat and persona choice is written in the AU vocabulary and bounded by the basic-emotions honesty rule, the Duchenne/restraint register and the muted-legibility constraint; the four emotional beats (awe, curiosity gap, tension-release, aspiration) and the show-not-tell/body-language craft come next because they are the sourced material a performance draws on; the status/persona layer (quiet-luxury register, aloofness, the closed likeness lane, voice delivery, per-persona signatures and dual-persona interplay) then calibrates that material to the two specific personas; and the open-loop ending and the per-beat performance-brief composition come last because they compose every upstream node into the muted-legible, honesty-gated, no-real-person deliverable the prompt-craft specialist consumes.

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any emotion or engagement claim
dominance_rules.rationale: the basic-emotions debate is unresolved and the muted-viewing figure is a tagged 2016 publisher number, so nothing may be stated as settled universal fact
dominance_rules.trigger: an emotion-universality claim or an engagement statistic is about to be stated
dominance_rules.action: direct AU mechanics with the emotion word as shorthand only, and quote engagement figures at the exact tag the research carries

dominance_rules.rule: Muted legibility dominates any audio-carried meaning
dominance_rules.rationale: a large majority of first-exposure viewing is muted, so a story that needs sound fails for most viewers
dominance_rules.trigger: meaning is about to be carried by a voiceover or sound cue
dominance_rules.action: carry all load-bearing meaning visually and in captions and keep audio a sound-on bonus

dominance_rules.rule: The no-real-person guardrail dominates any concealment or archetype device
dominance_rules.rationale: the closed likeness lane stays closed - concealment must never evoke a specific named real person
dominance_rules.trigger: a face-concealing device or archetype starts to steer toward a recognizable individual
dominance_rules.action: stop the brief and keep every persona an original fictional character

dominance_rules.rule: The AU6 eye-involvement direction dominates a lip-only smile
dominance_rules.rationale: the dead-eyed synthetic grin is the most recognizable AI tell and AU6 is the fix
dominance_rules.trigger: a warm smile is being directed
dominance_rules.action: name the AU6 cheek-raise/eye-crinkle component, not only AU12, at a restrained intensity

dominance_rules.rule: Restrained intensity dominates full expressiveness in the quiet register
dominance_rules.rationale: broad expression breaks the Patrician quiet-luxury read; restraint reads as class
dominance_rules.trigger: a beat (even high-arousal awe) is about to be directed at full intensity
dominance_rules.action: render the beat at restrained intensity with a floor of visible movement so it still reads

dominance_rules.rule: A payable open loop dominates a never-filled gap
dominance_rules.rationale: a curiosity gap that is never filled anywhere is clickbait that erodes trust
dominance_rules.trigger: an open-loop 'part 2' ending is being chosen
dominance_rules.action: open only a loop the series will pay off across posts and track the promised continuation

dominance_rules.rule: Coherent face-and-body authoring dominates separate authoring
dominance_rules.rationale: a calm face over a fidgeting body reads as incoherent and undercuts the status read
dominance_rules.trigger: facial AUs and body language are being specified
dominance_rules.action: author the face and body together so the AUs and the pace/posture/blink cues agree

dominance_rules.rule: Persona distinctness dominates register uniformity when they collide
dominance_rules.rationale: two personas that blur into one indistinct character lose the dual-persona value
dominance_rules.trigger: the two signatures read as the same character in review
dominance_rules.action: increase the rationed-warmth/gaze/pacing differentiators while keeping both in the quiet register

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the AU vocabulary and the label-as-shorthand honesty rule before writing any beat direction
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-writing every beat later to strip out over-claimed emotion labels and add the AU mechanics

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the AU6 eye-involvement component on every warm smile from the first brief
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering the dead-eyed grin across a batch and re-prompting all the smile beats

anti_rework_rules.rule: Anchor muted legibility before designing any beat or voiceover
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building an audio-dependent reel and having to re-cut it to work for the muted majority

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set a floor of visible movement when directing restrained micro-expression
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a batch of flat, emotionless faces that lose the beat and must be re-rendered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold the closed likeness lane closed from the first persona sketch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a concealment device that evokes a real person surfacing late and forcing a persona redesign

anti_rework_rules.rule: Synthesize the four beats into one palette before assigning per-persona signatures
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ad hoc signatures that contradict the sourced beats and need re-authoring for coherence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Author facial AUs and body language together per beat
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an incoherent calm-face-over-fidgeting-body read caught only after generation and re-shot

anti_rework_rules.rule: Only open a curiosity loop the series will pay off, and track the promised continuation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a never-filled 'part 2' that erodes trust and forces a credibility-repair series

iteration_protocol.trigger: a batch of generated output shows dead-eyed grins, flat under-rendered faces, or awe rendered as a broad gasp
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the AU6 direction, the restraint floor and the awe intensity, and update the affected beat/expression nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a brief is found depending on audio or evoking a specific real person at the composition gate
iteration_protocol.action: return the brief, restore muted-legibility and the no-real-person guardrail, and re-run the composition

iteration_protocol.trigger: the two personas read as indistinct or a signature drifts out of the quiet register
iteration_protocol.action: re-differentiate the signatures on rationed-warmth/gaze/pacing and re-confirm both stay in the Patrician register

iteration_protocol.trigger: the basic-emotions consensus shifts or a current primary-source muted-viewing statistic becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: update the debate and muted-legibility nodes and re-check every emotion/engagement claim against the new tag

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner clarifies what 'phonics' meant or the voice tooling constrains achievable delivery
iteration_protocol.action: revise the voice-delivery interpretation and its weight in the composed brief

iteration_protocol.trigger: an open-loop 'part 2' is found never paid off or a curiosity hook underperforms on retention
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the fillable-gap discipline and the open-vs-hard-loop choice and update the ending/curiosity nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new Higgsfield model changes how faithfully AU-level facial direction renders
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the AU vocabulary, the Duchenne lever and the restraint floor against the new model's fidelity
